purpose: Source provenance and citations for retrospective global Project Athena research.

citation.title: USGS Earthquake Catalog (ComCat) FDSN Event Web Service

notes: Athena preflights large requests with the count endpoint and adaptively partitions them below the service query limit.
ComCat is the operational event source; source/catalog coverage differences must remain visible in research metadata.
Use as an independent large-event reference and completeness cross-check, not as an unqualified substitute for ComCat.
Historical global completeness varies by time and magnitude; Athena's first frozen 50-year cohort therefore uses M6.0+.
GeoJSON is the source project's version-of-record format; record the source revision used for each Athena research bundle.
Retain original feature properties and source attribution when normalizing fault traces.
The source is global in scope but has documented geographic gaps; absence of a mapped nearby fault must never be interpreted as absence of active faulting.

citation.author: Peter Bird
citation.title: An updated digital model of plate boundaries
citation.formatted: Bird, P. (2003). An updated digital model of plate boundaries. Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems, 4, 1027. https://doi.org/10.1029/2001GC000252

notes: Athena uses the PB2002 digitization-step file because it explicitly records adjacent plate identifiers and seven source-defined boundary classes.
The pinned fraxen/tectonicplates mirror preserves the original PB2002 supporting data bytes used by Athena; scientific attribution remains Bird (2003).
The ODC-By-1.0 license recorded here applies to the pinned mirror collection; Athena preserves Bird (2003) citation and mirror provenance in generated artifacts.
Plate-boundary context is descriptive and retrospective. Proximity or plate-pair membership must not be interpreted as causal attribution or future-earthquake probability.
Athena treats only USGS Mw-family preferred magnitude types (Mw, Mww, Mwc, Mwb, Mwr, Mwp) as eligible for the scalar seismic-moment conversion.
Other magnitude types remain unconverted rather than being silently treated as Mw.

citation.author: Thomas C. Hanks; Hiroo Kanamori
citation.title: A moment magnitude scale
citation.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
citation.formatted: Hanks, T. C., & Kanamori, H. (1979). A moment magnitude scale. Journal of Geophysical Research, 84(B5), 2348-2350. https://doi.org/10.1029/JB084iB05p02348

notes: Athena uses the SI form Mw = 2/3 (log10 M0 - 9.1), equivalently M0 = 10^(1.5 Mw + 9.1) N m.
Scalar seismic moment is a source-size variable; it is not interpreted as energy delivered to another fault.

citation.author: James Dieterich
citation.title: A constitutive law for rate of earthquake production and its application to earthquake clustering
citation.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
citation.formatted: Dieterich, J. (1994). A constitutive law for rate of earthquake production and its application to earthquake clustering. Journal of Geophysical Research, 99(B2), 2601-2618. https://doi.org/10.1029/93JB02581

notes: This paper provides physical context for earthquake-rate changes and clustering after stress perturbations.
Athena interaction v1 does not implement a Dieterich rate-and-state inversion or infer stressing history.

citation.author: Geoffrey C. P. King; Ross S. Stein; Jian Lin
citation.title: Static stress changes and the triggering of earthquakes
citation.journal: Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America
citation.formatted: King, G. C. P., Stein, R. S., & Lin, J. (1994). Static stress changes and the triggering of earthquakes. Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America, 84(3), 935-953. https://doi.org/10.1785/BSSA0840030935

notes: This paper provides context for Coulomb static-stress triggering analyses.
Athena interaction v1 has no rupture geometry, slip model, receiver-fault orientation, or Coulomb stress calculation and therefore makes no static-stress attribution.

citation.author: Emily E. Brodsky; Stephanie G. Prejean
citation.title: New constraints on mechanisms of remotely triggered seismicity at Long Valley Caldera
citation.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
citation.formatted: Brodsky, E. E., & Prejean, S. G. (2005). New constraints on mechanisms of remotely triggered seismicity at Long Valley Caldera. Journal of Geophysical Research, 110, B04302. https://doi.org/10.1029/2004JB003211

notes: This work documents dynamic triggering and cautions that cumulative shaking energy density alone does not explain the observed remote triggering at Long Valley.
Athena interaction v1 therefore does not label scalar moment or catalog association as transferred energy or causal dynamic triggering.
